thread.title: Is Apple Making An IPhone Mistake? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Bill Maurer
title: Is Apple Making An IPhone Mistake? - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Ever since its debut in 2016, I've been a big fan of Apple's ( AAPL ) iPhone SE. I personally prefer the smaller size for carrying around, but there are others who like the cheaper price tag. Given the phone is now quite outdated, there have been many rumors about a potential update to the phone this fall. Unfortunately, one firm recently suggested this won't be happening, which I think would be a mistake.
Recently, there was some confusion over a BlueFin Research report. Originally, it seemed like the firm was saying that the iPhone SE was going to be discontinued this fall. However, a clarification since suggests that the SE will remain, but Apple has nixed plans for the SE 2. That would mean those who originally bought the phone back in 2016 and are eligible to upgrade now would have to find another option.
The iPhone SE was never designed to be a top of the line model, but it still boasted some nice specs. It contained the same A9 processor and primary camera that were found in the newest iPhone line at that point, the 6s. Everyone knows though that each year brings more technology improvements, and the table below shows a comparison to two of last year's new iPhones.
( Source: gsmarena, SE specs seen here )
We don't know the specs yet for this year's set of new iPhones, but they will feature the A12 processor which will be three generations better than the iPhone SE. Even if Apple wanted to skimp a little to lower product costs, a second generation SE could at least get a processor upgrade to the A11, with perhaps more memory, more base storage, and better cameras.
I could understand not refreshing the SE if sales were poor, but by all accounts they are doing quite well for a non-premium phone. As the CIRP data details below, the SE was in the high single digits percentage wise for US sales mix in the March 2018 quarter, not bad for a phone nearly two years old at that point. Even if only about 4% of sales are the SE, you're still talking about 9 million or so annually, which isn't exactly peanuts. That would make it a $4 billion revenue generator, which as I pointed out in my latest article , would alone be much better than several prominent technology companies.
( Source: CIRP data on 9to5 Mac article, seen here )
If there is no refresh coming for the SE, I hope it is because of some technical issues or not enough production capability. I would hope it isn't because Apple is trying to generate even higher average selling prices, moving consumers to more and more expensive iPhones. There already are rumors that this year's set of new phones will be more costly than last year's. While that could push average selling prices closer to $800, total iPhone revenues might not rise as much as the ASP gain if unit sales decline.
While it isn't the end of the world if Apple doesn't launch a second generation iPhone SE, it would be a disappointment for those like me who prefer the smaller form factor and/or lower price. It also does take down the potential a little for the company's biggest launch cycle ever this year. While some that are looking for a new phone will go with Apple's larger screen devices, it's likely that consumers holding the SE now will hold on longer. Apple could have generated millions more in upgrades, but that might not happen now. Less overall unit sales also can hurt other areas like Apple services.
In the end, there should be some disappointment among Apple consumers and investors if the iPhone SE doesn't get refreshed. While the phone isn't critical to the company's success, it fills a certain niche in the smartphone space and likely generates a few billion in annual revenues. Hopefully, this is either a technical or production issue at this point, and not an effort to push consumers to more expensive phones. That strategy won't work when the next economic downturn hits.
